rule: A protocol is verified only when the retrieved source states the dose under the heading for that indication and the contraindications and dose limits in that source were recorded. Finding a BNF, NICE, CKS or SmPC page is not verification. A dose is not copied from another indication. If the source does not support the pair, the pair stays unverified.

catalogueGaps.note: Dimenhydrinate is not an OSIRIS pharmacopeia record, so no guideline protocol is attached. Supported antihistamine records are cetirizine, loratadine, desloratadine, fexofenadine, diphenhydramine, chlorphenamine, hydroxyzine and promethazine. Those records do not yet have a verified protocol.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: NICE NG136, last updated 26 February 2026, offers step 1 treatment as an ACE inhibitor or an ARB for adults with type 2 diabetes of any age or family origin, and for adults under 55 who are not of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin. It offers a calcium-channel blocker for adults aged 55 or over without type 2 diabetes, and for adults of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin without type 2 diabetes. If an ACE inhibitor is not tolerated, for example because of cough, it offers an ARB. It says do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB. If a calcium-channel blocker is not tolerated, for example because of oedema, it offers a thiazide-like diuretic. If starting or changing diuretic treatment, it offers a thiazide-like diuretic such as indapamide in preference to a conventional thiazide such as bendroflumethiazide or hydrochlorothiazide. For adults of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin, consider an ARB in preference to an ACE inhibitor. For this ARB, the CKS hypertension table gives the adult oral doses below. Other ARBs in the same table are alternatives for hypertension, not additional medicines to combine with it.

standardDosing.startingDose: 50 mg once a day. Low starting dose when adverse effects are more likely: 25 mg once a day.
standardDosing.duration: Continued for as long as antihypertensive treatment remains indicated. The CKS page does not set a fixed stop date.
standardDosing.titration: NICE CKS hypertension, angiotensin-II receptor blockers, revised June 2026, says start with a low dose and titrate upwards every 4 weeks until the target blood pressure is reached or the maximum tolerated dose is reached. The CKS table cites BNF 2022. Lower starting doses in that table are for people more prone to adverse effects, such as elderly, frail or renally impaired people, or people taking a diuretic. Usual maintenance dose: 50 mg once a day. Maximum dose: 100 mg once a day.
alternatives: Same CKS table, hypertension only: candesartan, irbesartan, olmesartan, telmisartan, valsartan. Azilsartan and eprosartan are also in that table but are not OSIRIS pharmacopeia records.

NICE NG136 also offers a calcium-channel blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic such as indapamide at later steps, or a calcium-channel blocker at step 1 in the groups named above. Those class options are not given milligram doses here.

guidelineModifiers: Pregnancy or planning pregnancy: NICE NG136 points to MHRA advice that ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor antagonists are not for use in pregnancy.
CKS: ARBs are contraindicated with aliskiren in diabetes or when eGFR is below 60 mL/min/1.73 m².
CKS: do not combine an ARB with an ACE inhibitor for hypertension (NICE NG136 recommendation 1.4.34).
Volume depletion or a continued diuretic: CKS advises a low starting dose; people on a high-dose diuretic (equivalent to furosemide 80 mg or more) are referred to secondary care to start an ARB.
monitoring: Measure renal function (serum creatinine and eGFR) and serum electrolytes before starting treatment.
Check renal function and serum electrolytes 1–2 weeks after starting and 1–2 weeks after each dose increase, then annually unless clinical judgement indicates more frequent testing.
Check blood pressure 4 weeks after each dose titration.

For people at higher risk of hyperkalaemia or deteriorating renal function, including peripheral vascular disease, diabetes, pre-existing renal impairment, diuretics or older people, consider checking renal function and electrolytes within 1 week.

CKS, citing NICE, says some rise in creatinine and potassium is expected. If eGFR falls by 25% or more, or serum creatinine rises by 30% or more, look for another cause such as volume depletion or an NSAID. If none is found, stop the renin-angiotensin antagonist or return to a previously tolerated lower dose.

CKS says stop the renin-angiotensin antagonist in CKD if serum potassium reaches 6.0 mmol/L or more and other medicines that promote hyperkalaemia have been stopped. If potassium rises above 5.5 mmol/L, follow local guidance.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: NICE NG136, last updated 26 February 2026, offers step 1 treatment as an ACE inhibitor or an ARB for adults with type 2 diabetes of any age or family origin, and for adults under 55 who are not of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin. It offers a calcium-channel blocker for adults aged 55 or over without type 2 diabetes, and for adults of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin without type 2 diabetes. If an ACE inhibitor is not tolerated, for example because of cough, it offers an ARB. It says do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB. If a calcium-channel blocker is not tolerated, for example because of oedema, it offers a thiazide-like diuretic. If starting or changing diuretic treatment, it offers a thiazide-like diuretic such as indapamide in preference to a conventional thiazide such as bendroflumethiazide or hydrochlorothiazide. For adults of Black African or African-Caribbean family origin, consider an ARB in preference to an ACE inhibitor. Ramipril is one ACE inhibitor option. The adult oral dose below is from the UK SmPC, not from a milligram figure in NG136.

standardDosing.route: Oral. Swallow with liquid. Do not crush or chew. May be taken before, with or after meals. Take at the same time each day.
standardDosing.startingDose: 2.5 mg once daily.
standardDosing.duration: Continued while treatment for hypertension remains indicated. The SmPC does not set a fixed course length.
standardDosing.titration: The dose can be doubled at intervals of two to four weeks to reach the blood-pressure target. Maximum 10 mg daily.
alternatives: SmPC: if the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system is strongly activated, start at 1.25 mg once daily under medical supervision.
SmPC: if a diuretic is not stopped, start at 1.25 mg and monitor renal function and serum potassium. Where possible, stop the diuretic 2 to 3 days before starting ramipril.

NICE NG136: if the ACE inhibitor is not tolerated, offer an ARB. Do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB. A calcium-channel blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic such as indapamide is the alternative class at the steps described above. NG136 does not give ramipril milligram alternatives.

guidelineModifiers: SmPC renal impairment, creatinine clearance at least 60 mL/min: initial dose 2.5 mg daily, maximum 10 mg daily.
SmPC creatinine clearance 30–60 mL/min: initial dose 2.5 mg daily, maximum 5 mg daily.
SmPC creatinine clearance 10–30 mL/min: initial dose 1.25 mg daily, maximum 5 mg daily.
SmPC haemodialysis: initial dose 1.25 mg daily, maximum 5 mg daily, given a few hours after haemodialysis.
SmPC hepatic impairment: start only under close medical supervision. Maximum 2.5 mg daily.
SmPC elderly: consider a reduced initial dose of 1.25 mg, with more gradual titration, especially in very old and frail patients.
SmPC: safety and efficacy in children have not been established. No paediatric dose is recommended.
NICE NG136 / MHRA: ACE inhibitors are not for use in pregnancy.
monitoring: SmPC: assess renal function before and during treatment and adjust the dose especially in the first weeks. Particularly careful monitoring is required in renal impairment.
SmPC: when a diuretic is continued, monitor renal function and serum potassium.
SmPC does not state a routine serum-potassium interval for uncomplicated hypertension. No extra interval has been added.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The UK SmPC licenses ramipril for symptomatic heart failure. protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The catalogue indication ckd_progression is broader than the SmPC wording. The SmPC licenses ramipril for renal disease in three defined populations: incipient glomerular diabetic nephropathy with microalbuminuria; manifest glomerular diabetic nephropathy with macroproteinuria and at least one cardiovascular risk factor; and manifest glomerular non-diabetic nephropathy with macroproteinuria of at least 3 g/day. The doses below are those SmPC populations. They are not a single dose for every cause of chronic kidney disease.

standardDosing.startingDose: Depends on which SmPC population applies. See alternatives. Do not choose one starting dose when the population is not known.
standardDosing.frequency: Once daily in the schedules below.
standardDosing.duration: The SmPC does not set a fixed course length.
standardDosing.titration: Follow the population-specific schedule. Do not use the hypertension maximum as a substitute when the renal-disease population is unidentified.
alternatives: Diabetes with microalbuminuria: start 1.25 mg once daily. Double to 2.5 mg after two weeks, then to 5 mg after a further two weeks, if tolerated.

Non-diabetic nephropathy with macroproteinuria of at least 3 g/day: start 1.25 mg once daily. Double to 2.5 mg after two weeks, then to 5 mg after a further two weeks, if tolerated.

guidelineModifiers: If the person does not fall into one of the three SmPC populations, this protocol does not supply a dose.

NICE NG136 / MHRA: ACE inhibitors are not for use in pregnancy.
monitoring: SmPC: assess renal function before and during treatment and adjust the dose especially in the first weeks.
SmPC: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers should not be used together in diabetic nephropathy.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The UK SmPC licenses propranolol for the control of hypertension. NICE NG136 does not use a beta-blocker as routine step 1 treatment. Its resistant-hypertension step says that if potassium is above 4.5 mmol/L, an alpha-blocker or a beta-blocker may be considered. Propranolol is one non-selective beta-blocker. The milligram schedule below is the SmPC hypertension schedule, not an NG136 first-line recommendation.

alternatives: NICE NG136 step 1 alternatives are an ACE inhibitor, an ARB, a calcium-channel blocker, or a thiazide-like diuretic such as indapamide, in the groups already described. Those are class alternatives. This library does not add milligram doses for them here.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The UK SmPC indicates digoxin for chronic cardiac failure when the dominant problem is systolic dysfunction, with greatest benefit when the ventricle is dilated, and specifically when cardiac failure is accompanied by atrial fibrillation. Adult maintenance for most patients with heart failure is 125 to 250 micrograms daily, with 62.5 micrograms daily or less if sensitivity to adverse effects is increased. NICE NG196 tells clinicians to follow the chronic heart failure guideline for beta-blockers and for avoiding calcium-channel blockers when atrial fibrillation and heart failure coexist. This protocol does not replace that heart-failure pathway.

standardDosing.route: Oral for the schedules quoted. Intravenous digoxin is a different bioavailability: if switching from oral to intravenous, the SmPC says reduce the dose by about 33 percent.
standardDosing.startingDose: Individual. Suggested doses are an initial guide only. Rapid oral loading, if medically appropriate: 750 to 1500 micrograms (0.75 to 1.5 mg) as a single dose. Where there is less urgency, or greater risk such as in the elderly, give the oral loading dose in divided doses six hours apart, with about half the total as the first dose, and assess the clinical response before each further dose.
standardDosing.frequency: Maintenance is described as a daily dose. Loading doses are divided when the rapid single dose is not appropriate.
standardDosing.duration: The SmPC does not set a fixed course length. Maintenance follows loading.
standardDosing.titration: Slow oral loading, for example in mild heart failure: 250 to 750 micrograms daily for one week, then an appropriate maintenance dose. A clinical response should be seen within one week. The choice between slow and rapid loading depends on the clinical state and the urgency. Maintenance for most patients with heart failure is 125 to 250 micrograms daily. If sensitivity to adverse effects is increased, 62.5 micrograms daily or less may suffice. Some patients need a higher dose. The SmPC also gives a creatinine-clearance formula for daily loss and says these formulae cannot be used for creatinine clearance in children.

guidelineModifiers: SmPC renal impairment: reconsider both initial and maintenance doses when renal clearance of digoxin is reduced.

SmPC thyroid disease: reduce initial and maintenance doses when thyroid function is subnormal. In hyperthyroidism there is relative resistance and the dose may have to be increased, then reduced as thyrotoxicosis comes under control.

SmPC contraindications include intermittent complete heart block, second-degree atrioventricular block, arrhythmias caused by glycoside intoxication, accessory-pathway supraventricular arrhythmias such as Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome unless the pathway has been evaluated, ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy unless atrial fibrillation and heart failure coexist, in which case caution is still required.
BNF cautions include hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, hypercalcaemia and hypoxia because they increase toxicity.
monitoring: SmPC: doses must be tailored to age, lean body weight and renal function.
SmPC: if a cardiac glycoside was taken in the preceding two weeks, reconsider the initial dose and use a reduced dose.
SmPC elderly: take reduced renal function and lower lean body mass into account, reduce the dose if necessary, check serum digoxin levels regularly, and avoid hypokalaemia.
BNF: for a plasma-digoxin concentration, take blood at least 6 hours after a dose. Monitor serum electrolytes and renal function. Toxicity is increased by electrolyte disturbance.

standardDosing.startingDose: Immediate-release: 2.5 mg once daily in the morning. Prolonged-release: 1.5 mg once every 24 hours, preferably in the morning, swallowed whole with water and not chewed.
standardDosing.duration: The blood-pressure effect of the 2.5 mg tablet may continue for several months. Neither SmPC sets a fixed stop date. The 2.5 mg SmPC says there is no evidence of rebound hypertension on withdrawal.
standardDosing.titration: Do not increase the immediate-release dose above 2.5 mg daily: the SmPC says there is no appreciable extra antihypertensive effect and a diuretic effect may appear. If blood pressure is not controlled, add another antihypertensive class.
alternatives: The 1.5 mg prolonged-release tablet is not a lower dose of the 2.5 mg immediate-release tablet. Do not halve or substitute one product for the other from this record.

guidelineModifiers: SmPC contraindications for the 2.5 mg tablet include hypersensitivity to indapamide or other sulfonamides, severe renal failure (creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min), hepatic encephalopathy or severe hepatic impairment, hypokalaemia, porphyria, Addison's disease, and refractory hypokalaemia, hyponatraemia or hypercalcaemia.

Thiazide-like diuretics are fully effective only when renal function is normal or only minimally impaired. Elderly people can be treated when renal function meets that limit. The plasma creatinine used for that judgement must be adjusted for age, weight and sex.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The SmPC indication is type 2 diabetes mellitus, particularly in overweight patients, when diet and exercise alone do not give adequate glycaemic control. In adults it may be used alone, with other oral antidiabetic agents, or with insulin. A NICE guideline milligram schedule was not verified in this batch, so the dose below is the licensed SmPC dose only.

standardDosing.startingDose: Adults with GFR at least 90 mL/min: 500 mg or 850 mg two or three times daily. This is not a once-daily adult start.
standardDosing.frequency: Two or three times daily with meals for the adult start. The maximum is taken in three divided doses.
standardDosing.duration: Continued for type 2 diabetes while it remains indicated and renal function allows it. The SmPC does not set a fixed stop date.
standardDosing.titration: After 10 to 15 days, adjust on blood glucose. A slow increase may improve gastrointestinal tolerability. Maximum 3 g daily in three divided doses when GFR is at least 60 mL/min. At GFR 45 to 59 the maximum is 2 g daily and the starting dose is at most half the maximum. At GFR 30 to 44 the maximum is 1 g daily.
alternatives: Children from 10 years and adolescents: the SmPC start is 500 mg or 850 mg once daily, maximum 2 g daily. That once-daily start is not the adult start.
With insulin, the SmPC uses the same adult metformin start and adjusts the insulin on blood glucose.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The SmPC indication is stable mild and moderate chronic heart failure in addition to standard therapies in patients aged 70 years or older. The patient must have had no acute failure for six weeks. Other cardiovascular medicines must have been stable for two weeks. The start is 1.25 mg, not the 5 mg hypertension dose.

standardDosing.startingDose: 1.25 mg once daily.
standardDosing.duration: Generally long-term. Do not stop abruptly. If stopping, halve the dose weekly.
standardDosing.titration: At 1 to 2 week intervals, if tolerated: 2.5 mg once daily, then 5 mg once daily, then 10 mg once daily. Maximum 10 mg once daily. Each initiation and increase is supervised for at least 2 hours.
alternatives: If adverse effects prevent the maximum, stay at the tolerated step or reduce. Severe hypotension, acute pulmonary oedema, cardiogenic shock, symptomatic bradycardia or AV block: stop immediately.

guidelineModifiers: Hepatic insufficiency: the SmPC contraindicates nebivolol because data are limited.
Heart-failure use is restricted to stable mild and moderate chronic heart failure in patients aged 70 years or older, added to standard therapies. It is not a general adult heart-failure dose.
Angina and arrhythmia are not indications in section 4.1 of this SmPC.

The physician should be experienced in chronic heart failure. There is no experience in severe renal insufficiency, serum creatinine 250 micromol/L or more, so use is not recommended there. Mild to moderate renal insufficiency needs no separate adjustment because the titration is individual.
monitoring: At each increase, for at least 2 hours: blood pressure, heart rate, conduction disturbance and signs of worsening heart failure.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: Section 4.1 licenses atorvastatin, with diet, for primary hypercholesterolaemia including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, mixed hyperlipidaemia, and homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia when other lipid-lowering treatment is unavailable or insufficient. The primary-hypercholesterolaemia heading says most adults are controlled on 10 mg once daily. The cardiovascular-prevention heading is a different dose statement and is not used here.

standardDosing.route: Oral, once daily, with or without food, while a cholesterol-lowering diet continues.
standardDosing.startingDose: 10 mg once daily for primary hypercholesterolaemia and mixed hyperlipidaemia. Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia also starts at 10 mg daily.
standardDosing.duration: A response is usually seen within 2 weeks and the maximum response within 4 weeks. No stop date is set.
standardDosing.titration: Adjust at intervals of 4 weeks or more. Maximum 80 mg once daily. In heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, individualise up to 40 mg, then either 80 mg or 40 mg plus a bile-acid sequestrant. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: 10 to 80 mg daily, with other lipid-lowering treatment when that treatment is available.
alternatives: Paediatric heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia from age 10: start 10 mg daily. That schedule is not the adult primary-prevention dose.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in pregnancy and during breast-feeding. People who could become pregnant need effective contraception.

Check liver enzymes before the start and if symptoms suggest liver injury. Active liver disease, or unexplained transaminases above 3 times the upper limit, is a contraindication. Stop or reduce the dose if a rise above that limit persists.
Ask about unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness. The risk is higher with interacting medicines, higher doses, hypothyroidism and renal impairment.

Do not exceed 20 mg daily with elbasvir/grazoprevir or with letermovir. Atorvastatin is contraindicated with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, and is not recommended when letermovir is combined with ciclosporin.
No dose adjustment is stated for renal impairment. Use caution in hepatic impairment.
monitoring: Lipids after at least 4 weeks.
Liver enzymes before treatment and if liver injury is suspected.
Muscle symptoms, and creatine kinase if those symptoms appear.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The catalogue indication covers more than one prevention pathway, and the sources do not use one dose. The SmPC prevention heading says the dose in the primary-prevention trials was 10 mg daily, with the licensed maximum 80 mg. NICE NG238, published 14 December 2023, recommendation 1.6.7 offers atorvastatin 20 mg for primary prevention when the 10-year QRISK3 score is 10% or more. Recommendation 1.7.2 offers atorvastatin 80 mg for secondary prevention in people with cardiovascular disease, whatever the cholesterol, unless recommendation 1.7.3 applies: a drug interaction, a high risk of adverse effects, or a preference for a lower dose. The NG238 text states, immediately after those recommendations, that in December 2023 this was an off-label use of atorvastatin. Recommendation 1.8.1 offers atorvastatin 20 mg, not 80 mg, for primary or secondary prevention in people with chronic kidney disease. The SmPC 10 mg trial dose is not the NICE primary-prevention dose and is not the NICE secondary-prevention dose.

standardDosing.route: Oral, once daily, with or without food.
standardDosing.startingDose: Do not use a single dose for this indication. NICE NG238 primary prevention: atorvastatin 20 mg (recommendation 1.6.7, QRISK3 10% or more). NICE NG238 secondary prevention: atorvastatin 80 mg (recommendation 1.7.2), or a lower dose if recommendation 1.7.3 applies. NICE NG238 chronic kidney disease: atorvastatin 20 mg for primary or secondary prevention (recommendation 1.8.1). SmPC primary-prevention trial dose: 10 mg daily. That is not the NICE-preferred dose.
standardDosing.duration: No stop date is stated.
standardDosing.titration: NG238 aims for more than a 40% reduction in non-HDL cholesterol in primary prevention, and LDL cholesterol of 2.0 mmol/L or less, or non-HDL cholesterol of 2.6 mmol/L or less, in secondary prevention. In chronic kidney disease with eGFR at least 30, NG238 recommendation 1.8.2 says the atorvastatin dose may be increased if the lipid target is not met. The SmPC maximum remains 80 mg once daily.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in pregnancy and during breast-feeding. People who could become pregnant need effective contraception.

Check liver enzymes before the start and if symptoms suggest liver injury. Active liver disease, or unexplained transaminases above 3 times the upper limit, is a contraindication. Stop or reduce the dose if a rise above that limit persists.
Ask about unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness. The risk is higher with interacting medicines, higher doses, hypothyroidism and renal impairment.

This heading is primary prevention in high-risk adults. It is not a dose for someone who already has the familial-hypercholesterolaemia schedule, and it is not the 20 to 40 mg simvastatin prevention dose.
monitoring: Lipids if the dose is increased to reach a guideline LDL target.
Liver enzymes before treatment.
Muscle symptoms.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: Section 4.1 licenses simvastatin, with diet, for primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia, and for homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia with other lipid-lowering treatment. standardDosing.route: Oral, as a single evening dose.
standardDosing.startingDose: 10 to 20 mg once daily in the evening. Start at 20 to 40 mg in the evening only when a reduction in LDL-cholesterol of more than 45 percent is required.
standardDosing.duration: No stop date is stated. Continue the cholesterol-lowering diet.
standardDosing.titration: Adjust at intervals of at least 4 weeks. The range is 5 to 80 mg daily. The 80 mg dose has the restriction recorded in the modifiers.
alternatives: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia: the recommended starting dose is 40 mg in the evening, with other lipid-lowering treatment when available.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in pregnancy and during breast-feeding. People who could become pregnant need effective contraception.

Check liver enzymes before the start and if symptoms suggest liver injury. Active liver disease, or unexplained transaminases above 3 times the upper limit, is a contraindication. Stop or reduce the dose if a rise above that limit persists.
Ask about unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness. The risk is higher with interacting medicines, higher doses, hypothyroidism and renal impairment.
80 mg is only for severe hypercholesterolaemia at high cardiovascular risk when lower doses have not reached the goal and the expected benefit outweighs the risk.
Do not exceed 20 mg daily with amiodarone, amlodipine, verapamil, diltiazem, or elbasvir/grazoprevir.
Do not exceed 10 mg daily with fibrates other than gemfibrozil or fenofibrate. Gemfibrozil, ciclosporin, danazol and potent CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated.
Creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min: doses above 10 mg daily need careful consideration.
With lomitapide, do not exceed 40 mg daily.
monitoring: Lipids at intervals of at least 4 weeks after a dose change.
Liver enzymes before treatment.
Muscle symptoms, particularly if an interacting medicine is added.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: Section 4.1 treats primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia, and homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, from the age of 6 years, as an adjunct to diet. The adult start under the hypercholesterolaemia heading is 5 or 10 mg once daily. Prevention has a different heading.

standardDosing.route: Oral, at any time of day, with or without food.
standardDosing.startingDose: 5 or 10 mg once daily. Choose the start from the cholesterol level, cardiovascular risk and the risk of adverse effects.
standardDosing.duration: Continue the cholesterol-lowering diet. No stop date is stated.
standardDosing.titration: Move to the next dose level after 4 weeks if needed. Consider 40 mg only for severe hypercholesterolaemia at high cardiovascular risk, particularly familial, when 20 mg has not reached the goal and follow-up will continue.
alternatives: Children with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia are dosed by age under a separate paediatric heading. Those doses are not adult doses.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in active liver disease, unexplained transaminases above 3 times the upper limit, severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min), myopathy, ciclosporin, and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir.

Start at 5 mg, and do not use 40 mg, in Asian patients, in moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min), in people over 70 years, and in people with predisposing factors for myopathy.

The 40 mg dose is also contraindicated with hypothyroidism, a personal or family history of hereditary muscle disorders, previous statin or fibrate muscle toxicity, alcohol abuse, and concomitant fibrates. Specialist supervision is recommended if 40 mg is started.
Known SLCO1B1 c.521CC or ABCG2 c.421AA: use half the usual dose and do not exceed 20 mg daily.
Contraindicated in pregnancy and during breast-feeding. People who could become pregnant need effective contraception.
Ask about unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness. The risk is higher with interacting medicines, higher doses, hypothyroidism and renal impairment.

Muscle symptoms.

standardDosing.startingDose: 75 to 150 mg once daily for long-term secondary prevention.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The licensed SmPC and the guideline pathway do not use the same starting dose. Aldactone section 4.1 lists congestive cardiac failure. NICE NG106 recommendation 1.4.1, marked 2025, offers a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist as a class for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and does not state a milligram dose. NICE CKS, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, last revised March 2026, states spironolactone 25 mg daily with a target of 50 mg daily. The BNF heading retrieved on 20 October 2026, 'Moderate to severe heart failure (adjunct)', is initially 25 mg once daily, then 50 mg once daily. The BNF also keeps a separate oedema heading of initially 100 mg once daily. The 25 mg schedule is the guideline-preferred disease-modifying start. The 100 mg schedule is the licensed oedema dose and is not that start.

standardDosing.route: Oral, once daily with a meal.
standardDosing.startingDose: Guideline-preferred heart-failure start: 25 mg once daily, target 50 mg once daily (NICE CKS March 2026 and the BNF moderate-to-severe heart-failure heading). Licensed SmPC oedema of congestive cardiac failure: 100 mg daily, range 25 to 200 mg. Licensed SmPC severe NYHA III to IV schedule: 25 mg once daily only if serum potassium is 5.0 mEq/L or below and serum creatinine is 2.5 mg/dL or below.
standardDosing.frequency: Once daily for the severe-heart-failure schedule. The oedema schedule may be single or divided.
standardDosing.duration: Maintenance is individual. No fixed stop date is stated.
standardDosing.titration: CKS and the BNF moderate-to-severe heading: increase from 25 mg to 50 mg once daily if tolerated. SmPC severe-heart-failure heading: if 25 mg is not tolerated, 25 mg every other day. Do not use the 100 mg oedema start, or the 400 mg aldosteronism test dose, as the guideline heart-failure start.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in acute renal insufficiency, significant renal compromise, anuria, Addison's disease, hyperkalaemia, and with eplerenone or another potassium-sparing diuretic.
Hyperkalaemia can be fatal. Do not add oral potassium or another potassium-sparing diuretic. ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs and heparin increase the risk.
Hypertension is not a section 4.1 indication of this SmPC. No hypertension dose is recorded.
monitoring: NICE CKS: renal function and electrolytes before the start, 1 to 2 weeks after the start, 1 to 2 weeks after each increase, then every 3 to 6 months, and whenever renal function may be compromised. Blood pressure before and after each increase.

SmPC severe-heart-failure heading: potassium and creatinine 1 week after the start or an increase, monthly for 3 months, quarterly for a year, then every 6 months. Stop or interrupt if potassium exceeds 5 mEq/L or creatinine exceeds 4 mg/dL.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The non-valvular atrial-fibrillation heading is prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adults with one or more named risk factors. The dose is 5 mg twice daily, reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two reduction criteria are present. The deep-vein-thrombosis treatment schedule is a different heading.

standardDosing.startingDose: 5 mg twice daily. Use 2.5 mg twice daily if at least two of these apply: age 80 years or older, weight 60 kg or less, serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL (133 micromol/L) or more.
standardDosing.duration: Long-term.
standardDosing.titration: No upward titration. Severe renal impairment, creatinine clearance 15 to 29 mL/min: 2.5 mg twice daily for this atrial-fibrillation indication.
alternatives: Before cardioversion in a person not already anticoagulated: at least five doses, using the reduced dose if the reduction criteria apply. A 10 mg load is a separate cardioversion instruction, not the chronic dose.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in active clinically significant bleeding, hepatic disease with coagulopathy and a clinically relevant bleeding risk, a lesion or condition at significant risk of major bleeding, and with another anticoagulant except during a defined switch or specified heparin use.
Not recommended with creatinine clearance below 15 mL/min or on dialysis. Not recommended with a prosthetic heart valve. Liver tests are required before the start.
Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Mild or moderate hepatic impairment needs no dose change but needs caution.
monitoring: Bleeding. Renal function, age and weight at the start so the 2.5 mg criteria are not missed. Liver tests before the start. No routine coagulation monitoring.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The prevention heading on this SmPC is prevention of recurrent deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism after treatment. Its dose is 2.5 mg twice daily, started only after 6 months of therapeutic anticoagulation. Acute treatment is 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily, and that treatment schedule is not the prevention dose. This page does not give an orthopaedic surgical-prophylaxis dose.

standardDosing.startingDose: 2.5 mg twice daily after 6 months of treatment with apixaban 5 mg twice daily or another anticoagulant.
standardDosing.duration: Individual, balancing further prevention against bleeding. Acute treatment of a transient risk is at least 3 months, but that duration belongs to the treatment heading.
standardDosing.titration: Do not start prevention at 10 mg. The 10 mg twice-daily dose is only the first 7 days of acute treatment.
alternatives: Acute treatment, which is a different heading: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily. It is recorded so it is not mistaken for prevention.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in active clinically significant bleeding, hepatic disease with coagulopathy and a clinically relevant bleeding risk, a lesion or condition at significant risk of major bleeding, and with another anticoagulant except during a defined switch or specified heparin use.

Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Mild or moderate hepatic impairment needs no dose change but needs caution.
For this treatment and prevention heading, severe renal impairment is caution rather than an automatic reduction to 2.5 mg. The atrial-fibrillation reduction rule is not copied across.
monitoring: Bleeding. Renal function and liver tests before the start.

guidelineModifiers: Pregnancy restrictions of an angiotensin-receptor blocker apply. History of angioedema needs the same caution as other agents in the class.
Combination of an ACE inhibitor, a potassium-sparing diuretic and candesartan is not recommended unless the benefit and risk have been weighed.
Do not combine an ACE inhibitor and an angiotensin-receptor blocker in diabetic nephropathy.
Heart-failure trials did not include serum creatinine above 265 micromol/L. Experience is limited when creatinine clearance is below 15 mL/min.
The 8 mg hypertension start is not the heart-failure start.
monitoring: Renal function, creatinine and potassium during titration, and periodically, especially at age 75 or older or when renal function is impaired.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The indication includes control of hypothyroidism. Adult starting doses are split by age and cardiac disease. A single 100 microgram start applies only to people under 50 years without the over-50 or cardiac headings.

standardDosing.route: Oral, preferably before breakfast or the first meal.
standardDosing.startingDose: Under 50 years: 100 micrograms daily. Over 50 years without cardiac disease: do not exceed 50 micrograms daily at the start. Cardiac disease: 25 micrograms daily or 50 micrograms on alternate days.
standardDosing.duration: Usually long-term replacement. No stop date is stated.
standardDosing.titration: Under 50, and over 50 without cardiac disease: increase by 50 micrograms every 3 to 4 weeks. Cardiac disease: increase by 25 micrograms every 4 weeks. Usual final daily dose is in the ranges 100 to 200, 50 to 200, or 50 to 200 micrograms respectively.
alternatives: A target named for younger patients without heart disease is a thyroxine level of 70 to 160 nanomol/L or TSH below 5 milliunits/L. Over 50, clinical response may be preferred to a serum target.
If metabolism rises too fast, including angina, stop for a day or two and restart lower.

guidelineModifiers: Not a dose for thyroid cancer suppression or for a non-toxic goitre. Those indications are not on this tablet's section 4.1.
Take a pre-treatment ECG because hypothyroid ECG changes can look like ischaemia.
Paediatric and neonatal doses are weight-based and are not adult doses.
monitoring: TSH, and clinical response, at each titration interval. ECG before treatment when cardiac disease is possible.

standardDosing.titration: Maintenance after healed reflux oesophagitis: 10 mg once daily, increased to 20 or 40 mg once daily if needed.
alternatives: A response to 10 mg daily is a reason to use that lower dose for symptomatic disease. It is not the severe-oesophagitis dose.

guidelineModifiers: Concomitant nelfinavir is contraindicated.
Swallow gastro-resistant capsules whole. Do not chew them.

standardDosing.route: Oral. Swallow the gastro-resistant capsule whole.
standardDosing.startingDose: Active duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, or NSAID-associated ulcer: 20 mg once daily. Poorly responsive duodenal ulcer: 40 mg once daily. Poorly responsive gastric ulcer: 40 mg once daily.
standardDosing.frequency: Once daily for those treatment courses. Eradication regimens are twice daily or three times daily for the antibiotics, as written in the SmPC.
standardDosing.duration: Duodenal ulcer: usually 2 weeks, or a further 2 weeks; poorly responsive disease usually 4 weeks at 40 mg. Gastric ulcer and NSAID-associated ulcer: usually 4 weeks, or a further 4 weeks; poorly responsive gastric ulcer usually 8 weeks at 40 mg. Eradication regimens: one week.
standardDosing.titration: Relapse prevention of duodenal ulcer when Helicobacter is absent or cannot be eradicated: 20 mg once daily, sometimes 10 mg, or 40 mg if that fails. Relapse prevention of poorly responsive gastric ulcer: 20 mg once daily, or 40 mg if needed.
alternatives: One-week eradication: omeprazole 20 mg with clarithromycin 500 mg and amoxicillin 1,000 mg, each twice daily; or omeprazole 20 mg with clarithromycin 250 or 500 mg and metronidazole 400 or 500 mg, each twice daily; or omeprazole 40 mg once daily with amoxicillin 500 mg and metronidazole 400 or 500 mg, both three times daily. Antibiotic choice follows local resistance.

guidelineModifiers: Concomitant nelfinavir is contraindicated.
Swallow gastro-resistant capsules whole. Do not chew them.
NSAID-ulcer prevention at 20 mg once daily is only for people at risk: age over 60, previous ulcer, or previous upper-gastrointestinal bleeding.
monitoring: Healing symptoms at the interval named for that ulcer type.
Confirm eradication if a Helicobacter regimen was used and symptoms continue.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The indication is type 2 diabetes in adults when diet, exercise and weight loss are not enough. This record is the immediate-release 80 mg tablet. A modified-release gliclazide dose was not the dose on this page.

standardDosing.route: Oral, with the main meals. The tablet can be halved.
standardDosing.startingDose: 40 to 80 mg daily, which is half to one 80 mg tablet.
standardDosing.frequency: Once daily until the daily dose exceeds 160 mg, then twice daily with the main meals. A single dose must not exceed 160 mg.
standardDosing.duration: Continued while type 2 diabetes treatment remains indicated. No fixed stop date is stated.
standardDosing.titration: Increase according to blood glucose. The total daily dose may be 40 to 320 mg.
alternatives: Switching from another oral agent usually starts again at 40 to 80 mg. A sulfonylurea with a long half-life may need a few treatment-free days first.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in type 1 diabetes, ketosis or acidosis, diabetic pre-coma or coma, severe renal or hepatic insufficiency, breast-feeding, hypersensitivity to sulfonylureas or sulfonamides, and with miconazole.
Prescribe only when meals, including breakfast, are regular. Hypoglycaemia can be severe and prolonged.
Use the same adult regimen from age 65. Mild or moderate renal impairment can use the same regimen with closer monitoring. Not established in children.
monitoring: Blood glucose during titration. Explain hypoglycaemia symptoms and treatment with carbohydrate.

protocols.guidelineDirectedTherapy: The indication is symptomatic treatment of asthma and other reversible airways obstruction, and prevention of exercise- or allergen-induced attacks. A short-acting beta-agonist is not the only asthma treatment. This dose is one 100 microgram inhalation from the pressurised inhaler, not a nebuliser and not an oral dose.

standardDosing.route: Inhaled from a pressurised metered-dose inhaler, 100 micrograms per puff. Sit or stand, and hold the inhaler upright.
standardDosing.startingDose: Relief: one inhalation of 100 micrograms, increased to two inhalations if needed. Prevention of exercise or allergen challenge: two inhalations 10 to 15 minutes beforehand.
standardDosing.frequency: As required. Do not usually repeat sooner than every 4 hours, and do not exceed 8 inhalations in 24 hours.
standardDosing.duration: Symptom relief. Increasing use means the asthma is poorly controlled and the preventer treatment needs review.
standardDosing.titration: No regular upward titration. Chronic use of more than the as-required relief dose is a sign to review treatment rather than a target dose.
alternatives: Children under 12: usually one inhalation for relief, or one inhalation before challenge, increased to two if needed.

guidelineModifiers: Contraindicated in hypersensitivity and for threatened abortion or premature labour.

emc 13548 section 4.1 lists essential hypertension and chronic heart failure in people aged 70 years or older. Angina is not an indication.
emc 13548 does not list arrhythmia as an indication. The heart-failure titration was not copied across.

A metoprolol succinate heart-failure SmPC was not retrieved, so the pair stays unverified.
